fieldValues.title: A real user's session is an occasion: it is reported, its findings enter intake, and its file is kept
fieldValues.move: When someone uses an SRS editor for real work (not dogfooding on the spec), the session that follows is recorded as an occasion: a run-report in the programme names the repository, the agents that wrote to it, what broke and the issues filed. Every issue it produces carries a group label and a priority the day it is filed, so it lands in a queue. Before agents write to a real user's file, a restorable snapshot is taken. Agent-damage findings (no change view, no undo of an agent's changes, a broken render that validates clean, writes with no createdBy) rank above polish in the group's queue.
fieldValues.does_not_fix: The editor features themselves (srs-web#587-#590, srs-rust#1423). How agents pace their help (remedy 800f223f). Dogfooding on the spec repositories, where git, gates and PRs already give diff, undo and validation.
fieldValues.falsifier: After the next two real sessions, a finding from them is still in no queue a week later, or a user's file cannot be restored to its state before the agents wrote.
source_ref: Work-flow audit 2026-10-23: the ENA contract session (2026-10-21) produced six problems; four landed unlabelled in no queue and the working group reported its queue dry; ena.srs was untracked
fieldValues.return_when: After the next real-use session, or when the editor gains its own snapshots.
